title: Add serializable mat4 transform operations
description: Expose JSCADs transforms.transform(matrix, shape) as a serializable operation, allowing callers to preserve an already-calculated placement without decomposing it into Euler angles or reconstructing a nested operation sequence.
body:
## Summary

Expose JSCAD's `transforms.transform(matrix, shape)` as a serializable operation:

```ts
{
  type: "transform",
  matrix, // 16 finite numbers, column-major
  shape,
}
```

This lets callers preserve an already-calculated placement, such as part-local to assembly-local, without decomposing it into Euler angles or reconstructing a nested operation sequence. The interpreter passes the matrix unchanged to the supplied JSCAD implementation.

## Scope and conventions

- Add `Matrix4`, `TransformOperation`, matrix validation, and `toTransformMatrix()` for lossless copying from numeric arrays and typed arrays into JSON-serializable tuples.
- Preserve nested rotate/translate/scale operations as useful geometry-construction APIs. This does not flatten Boolean trees, infer component frames, or attach matrix metadata to existing operations.
- Coordinate-frame meaning belongs to the caller. Matrices use JSCAD's column-major convention, with translation at indices 12-14.
- Keep `transforms.transform` optional on custom adapters. Legacy operations continue to execute without that method; a matrix operation reports an explicit capability error before evaluating its child. The concrete `jscadPlanner` export still guarantees a callable method.
- Correct `geom3.create` and `CreateGeom3Operation.polygons` to accept native polygon objects (`vertices`, optional color/plane), matching what the interpreter already forwards to JSCAD.

## Compatibility

Existing operation dispatch is unchanged. Plans containing the new `transform` operation require an updated interpreter: an older planner cannot execute them merely because native JSCAD supports matrices. Reader dependencies must be updated before producers send them matrix operations.

The polygon type correction narrows the TypeScript contract. Callers using raw vertex arrays must construct polygon objects, for example with `jscad.geometries.poly3.create(vertices)`; this PR does not add a runtime conversion.

No package version is manually bumped. Circuit JSON placement fields, aperture/mounting policy, and downstream reader dependency updates are outside this PR.

## Validation

- `bun test ./tests`: 16 passing tests, 102 assertions.
- `bunx --no-install tsc --noEmit`: passes.
- `bun run build`: passes, including declarations.
- Coverage includes native 2D/3D geometry, off-axis and nested transforms, JSON roundtrips, typed-array copying, invalid matrices, native polygon metadata, and custom adapters without matrix support.
- New exports pass the workspace duplicate-helper gate.

title: test: reproduce duplicate vias shared by same-net routes
description: Reproduces a bug where duplicate vias are emitted for same-net routes crossing PCB layers at the same position, establishing expected behavior for a future fix.
body:
When two routes on the same net cross PCB layers at the same position, core currently emits a separate `pcb_via` for each route. Both records describe one physical hole. Because the vias overlap exactly, the rendered PCB can look correct while Circuit JSON contains duplicate vias.

This PR adds a deterministic reproduction to document the bug and establish the expected behavior for a fix: retain both routed traces, but emit only one shared `pcb_via`. It connects one top-layer resistor to two bottom-layer resistors and forces both routes through `(0, 0)`. The second route traverses the layers in the opposite direction, so future via reuse must recognize the same physical via regardless of traversal direction.

The PCB snapshot documents the layout with the note “Shared via: one physical hole.” An explicit via-count assertion catches the duplicate records that are visually indistinguishable in the snapshot. The test uses `test.failing` to keep the suite green while the bug exists; remove `.failing` when shared-via reuse is implemented. This PR adds the reproduction only and does not fix production behavior.

Validation: `bun test tests/repros/repro-shared-route-via-duplicates.test.tsx` passes with the expected-failure marker (1 pass, 0 fail). `git diff --check HEAD^ HEAD` also passes.

description: Removes disconnected copper pour fragments that survive the solvers area filter by adding a cleanup phase after via stitching to ensure only connected pours remain.

Preserve small connected pours and manually authored vias, and remove generated stitching vias belonging to floating components. Geometry checks account for copper layers, holes, curved shapes, and trace widths rather than using an area cutoff.

Keep existing test fixtures unchanged. Update the AM62L fanout-comparison snapshot where completed routing leaves 51 isolated pour fragments; before/after circuit data confirms that only pour records change. Retain the nRF52810 island-removal assertion while preserving the main's existing test skip and snapshots for its known Pipeline9 clearance regression.

title: Normalize shared schematic terminals for switch routing and labels
description: Normalizes shared schematic terminals for internally connected pushbutton pads to prevent zero-length wires and improve label handling.
body:
Internally connected pushbutton pads could be routed as separate schematic terminals. Redundant pad-to-pad traces then produced zero-length wires that hid the ground connection. Partial terminal deduplication could also create both an inline label and a fallback anchored label at the same terminal.

Resolve physical-pad schematic ports to shared symbol terminals before building the routing problem. Use the same terminal IDs for solver pins, direct connections, net membership, and explicit-label handling. Propagate the displayed terminal's connected state to its physical aliases after both regular and inline traces are applied, before fallback labels are generated. Source ports and source traces remain intact.

Update PushButton to assign each symbol terminal to one physical owner, using resolved internal connections so numeric and named pin aliases work consistently. Four-pad switches retain four source-linked schematic_port records but present two terminals to the routing solver. Built-in schematic_component symbol metadata is preserved.

Regression coverage checks:
- Exactly one BOOT inline label and one GND label, visible wires, two solver terminals, and correct physical-port positions/directions.
- Numeric and named aliases, reversed internal-pair ordering, rotations, and explicit anchored labels.
- A resistor-to-switch trace path through both redundant pads retains its external connection and its three source endpoints.

Validation: 44 targeted tests pass, covering pushbuttons, custom symbols, multi-port paths, net labels, inline labels, and schematic sheets. Type checking and formatting pass. Updated schematic snapshots were rendered and visually inspected.

CI follow-up: skip the failing AM62L progressive fanout test as requested. The Arduino center-reroute PCB snapshot now allows a test-local 0.15% pixel difference: two Linux CI runs differed by 0.10% in the rerouted region while all 124 routing/geometry assertions passed, and the same test passed locally under Bun 1.3.2 and CI’s Bun 1.4.0. title: Reproduce opposite-side through-hole pin and courtyard overlap
description: Adds a test to reproduce the issue where through-hole display pins overlap with the courtyard of a battery holder on the opposite side of the PCB without reporting a placement issue.
body:
## Summary

This PR adds a connected PCB reproduction with two through-hole displays on the top side and a battery holder on the bottom side.

Ten display through-hole pads fall inside the battery holder's bottom-side courtyard, but `runAllPlacementChecks` reports no issue.

## Why this matters

Through-hole leads and their solder joints occupy the opposite side of the PCB. Placing a component in the same area can interfere with assembly or rework and may allow the leads to contact the component.

## Expected behavior

Report a placement or assembly-clearance warning when a through-hole feature from one component is inside another component's courtyard on the opposite PCB side. Ordinary opposite-side SMD placement should remain allowed.

title: fix: show AI descriptions for related packages
description: Fixes rendering of related package descriptions by falling back to AI-generated descriptions when manual descriptions are absent, ensuring consistent display across server-rendered and client-hydrated content.
body:
## Summary

- fall back to ai_description in hydrated related-package cards when no manual description exists
- apply the same fallback in the server-rendered related-package markup
- add regression coverage for AI-only descriptions, manual-description precedence, and HTML escaping

## Why

The registry stores manually authored descriptions and generated descriptions in separate description and ai_description fields. A large number of packages have no manual description but do have a useful AI-generated description, and the related-packages endpoint returns both fields.

The main package About section already displays description first and falls back to ai_description. Related-package cards did not follow that behavior: both the React component and the independent SSR renderer only checked description. As a result, AI-described packages appeared without any explanatory text in the Related Packages section, even though the API response contained a description and the same package showed it on its own page.

Both render paths need to be updated because related packages are emitted in the initial server-rendered HTML and then hydrated by React. Fixing only one path would leave inconsistent output before and after hydration and could cause visible content changes.

The fallback preserves the intended precedence: a manually authored description is shown when present, ai_description is used only when it is absent, and no description block is rendered when both are empty.

## Validation

- bun test bun-tests/package-page-ssr.test.js (20 passed)
- bun run typecheck
- Biome formatting check
- git diff --check

title: Add Altium project export
description: Adds Altium Project to runframes export menu, allowing users to export circuit designs as Altium-compatible project files in a ZIP format.
body:
Adds **Altium Project** to runframe's export menu. The shared export dispatcher passes the current Circuit JSON and sanitized project name to `circuit-json-to-altium`, then downloads `<project>_altium_project.zip` containing native `.PcbDoc`, `.SchDoc`, and `.PrjPcb` documents. It uses the existing download helper and loading/success/error toasts.

The converter is loaded lazily from a pinned Git dependency (`5bdb7d235ef896ddf9ac5c4f315c4d0ce07fdfb5`) because it is not yet published on npm. Its transitive serializer is overridden to the published `altiumts@0.0.59` distribution, avoiding Git prepare-script failures on clean installs. This matches the integration in https://github.com/tscircuit/cli/pull/4657 and https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit.com/pull/4842.

- Full Bun suite: 67 tests pass.
- New integration test covers menu registration, export dispatch, sanitized filename, ZIP MIME type, native PCB/schematic signatures, and project references.
- Type checking and formatting checks pass.
- `bun run build` passes, including standalone, standalone-preview, and library/declaration builds.
- Production export-module bundle tested in headless Chrome, including the actual ZIP download.

description: Avoids duplicate net lookups during DRC repair by pinning high-density-repair03 to a specific commit, ensuring existing repair behavior is preserved without changes to routing policies or DRC rules.

## Summary

Avoid duplicate net lookups during DRC repair by pinning `high-density-repair03` to `fd77be86b949a8de03d529b1e21aaf58a540350a`.

The pinned commit is the existing dependency revision `37d2b7af008c3a79c1a794e2ca307583a0f19c98` plus one focused change: fetch each net ID once in `sharesNet`. Existing repair behavior and fixes are preserved; no routing-policy, search-budget, or DRC-rule changes.

Only one dependency line changes. No solver files, tests, or benchmark tooling are added.

## Validation

- Installed the exact published Git pin in an isolated local validation directory and verified its complete `lib` source against the integration commit. Other consumer dependencies were reused locally; this is not a fresh full install.
- Five focused connectivity and Pipeline9 DRC tests pass.
- Production build, including TypeScript declaration generation, passes.
- Diff whitespace check passes. Local formatting was not run, following repository instructions.

## Performance evidence

An earlier same-machine Pipeline9 comparison on autorouter main `d1e664f2`, using the same repair03 source change, measured SRJ18 **sample 8 only**, three runs per version:

| Median | Main | With change | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Pipeline solve | 62.780 s | 56.753 s | 9.60% |
| Joint repair | 24.484 s | 19.703 s | 19.53% |

All six runs completed with identical routing output, 0 DRC errors, and 315 vias. These are prior local measurements, not full-suite results for the dependency pin. Full SRJ18 regression and performance validation remains pending.

title: Repair coupled clearance violations within the existing regional budget
description: Fixes coupled clearance violations in autorouting, improving DRC pass rate from 62.5 to 75.0 with reduced median runtime.

The dependency update also includes the corresponding physical geometry fixes; the autorouter's direct R03, high-density and hypergraph dependencies remain unchanged.

title: Compute Pipeline9 node probabilities from one pathing output
description: Calculates each high-density nodes failure probability by reusing the complete pathing output for every input node, improving performance without altering existing probability formulas or pipeline stages.

Pipeline9 calculates each high-density node's failure probability by rebuilding the complete pathing output for every input node. Large boards repeatedly pay for identical route conversion and lookup work before high-density routing starts.

Build the solved-node lookup once and calculate every probability from that output. This distills one performance improvement from #2447 into three files. Probability formulas, pipeline stages, dependency versions, clearances, and search budgets are unchanged.

The [same-machine SRJ18 comparison](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/34308681211) runs `/benchmark --same-machine --dataset 18` on main `207c4191` and this PR's `c4d639eb` sequentially on one runner:

| Measurement | Main | PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| DRC passing | 9/16 (56.3%) | 10/16 (62.5%) |
| Completion | 11/16 (68.8%) | 12/16 (75.0%) |
| Timeouts | 3 | 2 |
| Total sample time | 3034.1s | 2732.0s (-10.0%) |
| P50 time | 143.3s | 128.8s (-10.1%) |
| P80 time | 348.8s | 300.6s (-13.8%) |
| P95 time | 360.0s | 360.0s |

Sample 12 changes from a 360-second timeout to DRC passing in 346.5s. There are no regressed outcomes. All 11 samples that complete on both revisions retain identical DRC messages and via counts. These rates describe this paired run; the quality gain comes from completing an existing route within the unchanged deadline.

Validation: all CI checks pass, including the full test suite, TypeScript, and production build. The generic regression verifies identical node probabilities with one output conversion. A separate full native sample 6 comparison preserves every route, reference DRC result, and non-timing solver statistic while reducing runtime from 300.9s to 265.0s (-11.9%).

title: fix: collapse same-net cycles before shared-stub cleanup
description: Collapses redundant same-net cycles before shared endpoint stubs are trimmed, handling cycles formed by two same-net traces and enclosed loops within one routed trace while preserving existing checks.
body:
## Summary

- collapses redundant same-net cycles before shared endpoint stubs are trimmed
- handles both cycles formed by two same-net traces and enclosed loops within one routed trace
- keeps the existing label-preservation, collision, and visible-length checks

## Root cause

The original cycle-removal pass ran too late, after shared-stub cleanup had removed the common endpoint needed to recognize a two-trace cycle. After that order was fixed, one rectangle remained because it was formed entirely inside a single self-crossing trace, while the cleanup only compared separate traces.

## Fix

Run cycle collapse before shared-stub cleanup and include strict interior self-crossings as candidates. The self-crossing path is shortened at its existing intersection and is accepted only when it reduces visible same-net geometry and passes the existing label-safety checks.

The rule uses topology only. It has no component names, circuit-specific coordinates, arbitrary spacing values, or endpoint-touch special cases.

## Snapshot impact

- the merged repeated-power-rail repro loses both redundant rectangles
- the existing PMP11282 repro loses one additional enclosed self-crossing loop of the same type
- components, labels, and unrelated traces remain in place; no other snapshots change

## Verification

- focused unit and repro tests pass
- TypeScript check passes
- formatting and diff checks pass
- full suite passes: 349 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed

title: feat: detect scattered same-rail decoupling capacitors
description: Adds DecouplingCapacitorGroupingSolver to detect and report scattered same-rail decoupling capacitors in schematic analysis, improving schematic readability and organization.
body:
Trellis Core's CPU sheet spreads same-rail decoupling capacitors across long rows and separate clusters. Add `DecouplingCapacitorGroupingSolver` so the merged real schematic reports four scattered banks: P3V3, P1V8, P0V9, and P1V5.

Emit one `DecouplingCapacitorsNotCloseTogether` issue per bank, containing every member in `capacitorSchematicBoxes`. XML exposes `capacitorNames="C1, C2, C3, C4"`, the supply and return names, and the measured and recommended maximum gaps. There are no first/second capacitor fields. Sheet filtering, placement context, and issue artifacts use the complete group.

Identify parallel power-to-ground capacitors through electrical connectivity and explicit net or supply-pin metadata. Keep different returns, sheets, groups, and subcircuits independent. Report a bank when its largest gap between component bounds exceeds `max(4 schematic units, 3 × the largest capacitor dimension)`. This is a schematic readability heuristic; nearby neighbors do not make a widely spread bank compact.

Coverage includes the unchanged Trellis export with four isolated stacked snapshots, each showing one bank and its diagnostic below the schematic. The C1–C4 row at x = -6, -2, 2, 6 that was previously accepted in #41 now emits one group warning; a compact four-capacitor row passes. Boundary, connectivity, supply-pin, and schematic-scope tests cover the exclusions. Update the affected wireless-mouse and RP2040 snapshots as well.

Addresses the group API and real schematic repro concerns in [the #41 review](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/pull/41#pullrequestreview-5150086986) and [the #40 review](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/pull/40#discussion_r3965309465).

title: fix: escape XML attribute values
description: Fixes XML attribute serialization by ensuring that string values are properly escaped to prevent malformed attributes in emitted XML fragments.
body:
## Summary

- always escape string values written by the shared XML-style attribute formatter
- remove message-specific escaping bypasses from schematic issue serializers
- update the capacitor-orientation regression expectation and affected stacked SVG snapshots

## Problem

The analyzer emits a sequence of XML-style fragments. The capacitor-orientation message contains schOrientation="vertical", but the message previously bypassed attribute escaping. That creates a malformed attribute inside the fragment:

    message="Use schOrientation="vertical" on this capacitor..."

The quote before vertical closes the message value early. A strict XML validator reports InvalidAttr when the fragments are placed under a single root element.

The corrected fragment keeps the same message while encoding the inner quotes safely:

    message="Use schOrientation="vertical" on this capacitor..."

## Scope

This PR fixes attribute serialization inside the emitted fragments. It does not add a common root element, so the raw multi-section output remains an XML fragment sequence rather than a standalone XML document. It also does not change schematic placement, issue detection, or structured line items.

## Implementation

The shared addAttr helper already contains the required escaping logic. This PR removes the option to bypass that logic and routes every existing message attribute through the safe path. This also prevents future messages containing quotes, ampersands, or angle brackets from producing malformed attributes.

## Validation

- bun run format:check
- bun run typecheck
- bun test: 47 passed, 0 failed
- upstream main wrapped in one Analysis element: XML validation fails with InvalidAttr at the capacitor message
- this branch wrapped in one Analysis element: XML validation passes
- updated and passed all affected stacked SVG snapshots

title: Prefer vertical orientation for rail-connected two-pin components
description: Adds a solver to report horizontal two-pin components connected to power or ground, suggesting a vertical orientation to avoid obscuring rail branches.
body:
Horizontal two-pin components connected to power or ground obscure the usual vertical rail branches. Add `TwoPinComponentRailOrientationSolver` to report `TwoPinComponentShouldBeVertical` and suggest a ±90° rotation: power above, ground below. This covers the R1/R2 example discussed in #49 and applies to any component with two source pins and opposing horizontal schematic pins, with no component-type or resistance filter.

Recognition follows actual source connectivity and explicit power/ground net or pin attributes. It does not depend on net names or pull-resistor metadata. Rotation suggestions preserve the connected pin's identity, including on polarized parts.

### Behavior

- Report horizontal components whenever either pin connects to power or ground, including bypass capacitors and series supply components whose two ends are both power connections.
- Accept vertical components and horizontal components with no rail connection. For series supply components, prefer the supplying or explicitly declared rail over the load pin when choosing rotation direction.
- Skip shorted endpoints, conflicting rail declarations, and missing or ambiguous placements/ports.
- Prefer this rail-specific rotation over a duplicate `CapacitorSymbolHorizontal` warning in pipeline output. The existing capacitor analyzer still handles its other cases.
- Complement pull-resistor placement (position relative to the signal pin) and #44's two-pin orientation analyzer (180° trace-simplification flips, which exclude rail-connected components).

The rule relies on circuit-json's rail declarations. It suggests symbol orientation; it does not reroute wires or change connectivity.

### Layout coverage

Three new focused layouts use TSX and stack the schematic above analysis. The mixed examples cover a capacitor, diode, inductor, polarized power-to-ground capacitor, zero-ohm link, and LED; their pin geometry validates both +90° and -90° suggestions. L1 uses a visible GND symbol. The series example verifies that D4 is reported even though its load requires power, and that reversing source-port order still puts its VCC end upward.

| Horizontal rail connections: reported | Vertical rail connections: accepted | Signal inductor accepted; supply diode reported |

| ![Mixed horizontal two-pin components with orientation suggestions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/8c446cc12080d73e02e2e33f8b04a16f16440f46/tests/cases/__snapshots__/rail-connected-two-pin-orientation-horizontal.snap.svg) | ![The same components vertically oriented with no issues](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/8c446cc12080d73e02e2e33f8b04a16f16440f46/tests/cases/__snapshots__/rail-connected-two-pin-orientation-vertical.snap.svg) | ![Horizontal signal-series inductor accepted and horizontal supply diode D4 reported](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/8c446cc12080d73e02e2e33f8b04a16f16440f46/tests/cases/__snapshots__/two-pin-rail-orientation-series-control.snap.svg) |

The existing [horizontal R1/R2 repro](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/8c446cc12080d73e02e2e33f8b04a16f16440f46/tests/cases/__snapshots__/pull-resistor-readable-layouts-horizontal.snap.svg) now reports both resistors; its conventional vertical control remains accepted. title: Route dense plane fanouts around real copper
description: Fixes routing failure for dense plane fanouts around existing copper connections in the AM62L SoC area, ensuring all connections are routed correctly and validated without altering component positions or connections.
body:
## Summary

- stack this solver fix on the real TSX/copper reproduction in #201
- detect dense plane fanouts whose component area already contains foreign all-layer copper connected to one of the declared plane nets
- stage plane via reservations with the signal fanout, expand blocked plane candidate domains, and select the remaining plane sites jointly
- allow only plane-terminated branches in this staging path to share copper when their SRJ connectivity proves they are on the same electrical net
- keep component positions, source connections, route targets, obstacles, and solver limits unchanged

## Root cause

The real AM62L input contains through-all decoupling vias and capacitor pads inside the SoC fanout area. Unlike the earlier synthetic obstacle case, that copper carries real VSS/VDDS connectivity. The ordinary opposite-edge path committed the signal buses before coordinating enough plane escape sites, then treated plane branches that are already joined by the declared ideal plane as unrelated copper. That left no globally compatible set of 102 plane terminations.

The fix keys off the input's electrical-net metadata and applies the existing staged/joint reservation machinery to this topology. It does not recognize this board by IDs or coordinates and does not replace the solver output with stored positions.

## Result

The #201 test changes from the expected failure to:

- 135/135 connections routed
- 102 plane terminations
- output validation passes
- independent routed-copper DRC passes for all 135 traces and vias

body:
Pin names and numbers used generic `FONTID=2`, which native Altium ignores for pin text, leaving an oversized Times New Roman fallback. Its default name margin also placed opposing labels too far inside narrow components.

Export independently enabled `NAME_CUSTOMFONTID` and `DESIGNATOR_CUSTOMFONTID`, following [Altium’s pin presentation settings](https://www.altium.com/documentation/altium-designer/components-libraries/creating-schematic-symbol#pin-display-name-and-designator--position-and-font). Names default to Arial **3 pt**, matching Circuit JSON (`0.15 circuit units × 20`); numbers use Arial **4 pt** (`0.2 × 20`). A positive `display_pin_label_font_size` overrides only the name, rounded up to integer points with a 1 pt minimum. Existing text colors are retained.

Names use a custom margin of **-2** (`-(0.1 circuit units × 20)`), matching Circuit JSON’s inset from the component edge. The smaller name font restores a gap between opposing GPIO labels in the microcontroller preview. Pin numbers keep their existing position; component width, pin geometry, and electrical fields are unchanged.

title: feat: add styled parts to schematic text
description: Adds support for styled text parts in schematic text, allowing for partial active-low overlines while retaining a plain-text fallback.
body:
`schematic_text` currently has only a plain `text` value, so converters cannot preserve styling that applies to part of a label—for example, KiCad `~{RI}/CLK`, where only `RI` is active-low. This adds optional `text_parts` while retaining `text` as the complete plain-text fallback for consumers that do not render styled parts. Both `schematic_text.text_parts` and `schematic_port.display_pin_label_text_parts` use the same exported `SchematicTextPart` type and Zod schema, keeping their representation consistent.

**Motive:** Represent partial active-low overlines on the Circuit JSON element that owns and positions the displayed text.

## Example

```json
{
  "text": "RI/CLK",
  "text_parts": [
    { "text": "RI", "is_overlined": true },
    { "text": "/CLK" }
  ]
}
```

## Validation

- 325 repository tests pass
- TypeScript check passes
- Zod lint passes
- snake-case check passes

Used by [circuit-to-svg #708](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-to-svg/pull/708) and [kicad-to-circuit-json #183](https://github.com/tscircuit/kicad-to-circuit-json/pull/183).

title: Fix orientation analysis for two-pad LEDs and diodes
description: Fixes the orientation analysis for two-pad LEDs and diodes by implementing a canonical rotation family for axis-aligned pads, ensuring accurate pin 1 location inference.
body:
`analyzePcbPin1Location` returns `null` for an ordinary two-pad LED with pin 1 at (-0.749, 0) and pin 2 at (0.749, 0), including every right-angle rotation. Both sides of the single pad row match, so the topology filter never selects a frame. Core therefore cannot populate the inferred local/supplier pin-1 frames, and `circuit-json-to-pnp-csv` falls back to the authored rotation instead of applying a supplier offset.

Use a canonical rotation family for exactly two distinct, axis-aligned pads numbered 1 and 2. The same convention applied to local and supplier footprints recovers their relative 0/90/180/270-degree rotation, including a reversed LED. The side label is a convention for the degenerate row; it does not infer additional pad geometry or electrical polarity. Multi-pad ambiguity and missing/invalid two-pin geometry continue to return `null`.

Validation:
- New regression tests failed on the original implementation and pass with this change.
- Covers all four orientations and all 16 supplier/local orientation pairs, translated/reordered pads, rounding noise, and ambiguous inputs.
- Full suite: 113 tests pass, 4 snapshots.
- `bun run build`, `bunx tsc --noEmit`, and formatting checks pass.
- Checked the current PnP converter with the reported board's LED pad geometry and matching/reversed supplier fixtures: it preserves the authored rotation for matching frames and applies 180 degrees for reversed frames.

This fixes the shared inference gap, not the Gerber renderer. It requires a util release and downstream adoption; callers must enable part-orientation analysis and supply the supplier frame to the PnP converter. It does not establish JLCPCB's actual zero-degree frame for C965807 or replace pin-label/polarity validation. No blanket rotation is applied to LEDs, and no board files or generated manufacturing artifacts are included.

title: Add missing electrical role flags to pinAttributes
description: Extend pinAttributes with missing electrical roles using the existing optional boolean pattern.
body:
Extend pinAttributes with missing electrical roles using the existing optional boolean pattern.

- Add `isInput`, `isOutput`, `isBidirectional`, and `isPassive`.
- Add `canUseTriState` / `isUsingTriState`, `canUseOpenCollector` / `isUsingOpenCollector`, and `canUseOpenEmitter` / `isUsingOpenEmitter`, following the existing drive-mode pattern.
- Continue using `requiresPower` and `providesPower` for power input/output.

New fields preserve explicit true/false values and remain unset when omitted. No enum, aliases, inferred values, or cross-field validation are added. Existing attributes require no migration. Circuit JSON propagation and ERC conflict checking need downstream implementation.

Validation: 508 tests pass, including new flag parsing, rejection of non-booleans, isBidirectional support, existing-attribute compatibility, and compile-time checking. Type checking, formatting, package build, and all four required generation scripts pass.

title: Allow saved fanout trace paths to start and end with vias
description: Allows saved fanout trace paths to start or end with a via, including routes with vias at both endpoints, ensuring valid route shapes when circuit permits placement.
body:
Follow-up to #837: allow saved fanout trace paths to start or end with a via, including routes with vias at both endpoints. These are valid route shapes when the circuit permits the corresponding placement, such as via-in-pad.

Initialize layer continuity from a leading via's `from_layer` and advance to its `to_layer` as usual. Keep the minimum route length and reject discontinuous wire/via transitions. The standalone props schema does not have pad geometry or inherited `allowViaInPad` configuration, so placement permission remains a core concern.

Includes start-via, end-via, both-endpoint, consecutive-via, and invalid-continuity regression cases. All 486 tests pass, along with typecheck, build, and formatting. Ran all four required generators and included their output.

title: Add pcbTracePaths for reusable pre-generated fanout routes
description: Adds pcbTracePaths to BreakoutProps to store pre-generated port-to-exit routes as JSON, allowing for reuse without generating Circuit JSON IDs, while preserving existing automatic fanout defaults.
body:
Adds `pcbTracePaths` to `BreakoutProps` (used by `<breakout>` and `<fanout>`) so pre-generated port-to-exit routes can be stored as JSON and reused without generated Circuit JSON IDs. Exports `FanoutTracePath` and `fanoutTracePath`, with wire/via validation and unit-aware distances normalized to millimeters.

The prop is optional and preserves existing automatic fanout defaults. Its declaration documents the coordinate frame, physical layer semantics, automatic-routing precedence, and duplicate-exit restrictions. Runtime route placement and preservation are implemented in the companion core PR: https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/3809.

Validation: all 481 tests pass; typecheck, package build, and formatting pass. Ran all four required documentation generators and included the generated output.

title: fix: render overlined pin labels and schematic text
description: Fixes rendering of overlined pin labels and schematic text in SVG output for KiCad active-low formatting.
body:
KiCad active-low pin names and local wire labels are represented as structured text parts, but the SVG renderer previously understood only the legacy whole-label `N_` convention. This change renders `display_pin_label_text_parts` and `schematic_text.text_parts` as native SVG `<tspan>` elements, applying `text-decoration="overline"` only to parts marked `is_overlined`. A mixed label such as `RI/CLK` therefore receives one continuous overline over `RI`, while `/CLK` remains plain. A shared text-part renderer handles both fields without manual line geometry or positioning constants, while unstyled text and legacy `N_` labels retain their existing behavior.

**Motive:** Preserve KiCad active-low formatting through Circuit JSON and render it faithfully in schematic SVG output.

## Reproduction

The baseline reproduction was merged in [#721](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-to-svg/pull/721) using the unmodified Easyduino Circuit JSON generated by `kicad-to-circuit-json`. This PR updates that same test and snapshot to verify the fix: KiCad `~{...}` markup is absent, all 15 structured overline parts are rendered, and the partial `RI/CLK` label overlines only `RI`.

## Validation

- Uses the released `circuit-json@0.0.486` structured text-part schema from [circuit-json #769](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/769)
- 357 tests pass; 1 existing test remains TODO
- Package and TypeScript declarations build successfully
- Changed files pass Biome formatting and `git diff --check`

body:

## Intended result

The proposed renderer output adds continuous overlines to the marked text parts:

![Proposed circuit-to-svg output with active-low overlines](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hrithik18k/circuit-to-svg/feat/render-pin-label-text-runs/tests/__snapshots__/easyduino-overline.snap.svg)

In the intended image, inspect both kinds of text around pins 24, 28, and 11:

- the black external wire labels: `RTS`, `DTR`, and `SUSPEND`

Both sets have overlines. The change also overlines only `RI` in `RI/CLK` and only the active-low prefixes in labels such as `TXT/GPIO.0`; suffixes such as `/CLK` and `/GPIO.0` remain plain. The expected output follows the KiCad rendering in the [Easyduino conversion reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/kicad-to-circuit-json/main/tests/repros/easyduino-overline/__snapshots__/easyduino-overline.snap.png).

**Motive:** Capture the existing rendering failure with a real generated schematic before applying the renderer fix.

## Summary

- prevents an already-shortened trace from being treated as if it still starts at its original pin

## Root cause

The shared-endpoint cleanup stopped after collapsing the first duplicate stub. When three or more same-net routes shared a component port, another duplicate stub could remain and render a junction directly on the port.

The trace still retains its original pin metadata after a redundant prefix is removed, so continuing the scan also requires checking that the routed path still reaches that pin.

Continue checking the remaining same-net traces after a collapse, re-read the current first trace, and only process paths that still begin at the actual shared pin.

The rule uses existing trace topology. It has no component names, circuit-specific coordinates, new spacing constants, or renderer-only suppression.

A13 still spends most of its runtime in A* queue operations after #115. Move that hot loop into a synchronous WebAssembly kernel and reuse unchanged route-pair checks and goal heuristics. Routing policy, the 1.1 greedy multiplier, heap tie ordering, and physical clearances stay unchanged.

On the unchanged SRJ18 hard node at 1×, three warmed, alternating trials for each of five seeds show **2.10× aggregate speedup relative to merged #115 (`cdfd68a`)**. The kernel keeps 64-bit cost arithmetic and uses 16-byte heap entries with per-state versions for stale-entry detection. Each solver has independent memory. `searchBackend: "auto"` falls back to JS when WebAssembly/SIMD is unavailable or blocked; `"javascript"` and `"wasm"` can be selected explicitly. The generated module is embedded, so normal builds need no compiler, fetch, worker, or new dependency. Readable C source and an LLVM rebuild script are included. Heuristic caching is capped at 8 MiB per solver; the WASM buffers trade additional memory for speed.

title: Translate the A13 C kernel into JavaScript and compare performance
description: Translates the A13 C search kernel into JavaScript to evaluate performance without WASM execution, while maintaining the original functionality and structure.
body:
Translate the A13 C search kernel closely into JavaScript to test whether its gains survive without WASM execution. This PR is stacked on #116 so the diff isolates the translation.

`auto` and `javascript` now select the new JavaScript kernel. Explicit `wasm` remains available as the unchanged comparison backend. The default path never compiles or instantiates WebAssembly; the previous JS fallback/search loop is removed.

The translation preserves topology flags, push/pop tie comparisons, stale-entry versions, cost operation order, early rejection of non-improving neighbors, move visitation order, heap growth boundaries, and debugger stepping. Constructor closures replace C globals, scalar return fields avoid allocating temporary structs, and separate Float64/Int32/Uint32 arrays hold the same heap fields in 16 bytes per entry. Input arrays are referenced during a search instead of copied into linear memory. C source and WASM bytes remain unchanged for comparison.

### Results

**The full WASM speedup is not retained.** Three warmed, alternating trials per seed across five seeds show:

- **1.68× WASM's runtime** (about 68% longer). Seed 0: WASM 0.570 s, JavaScript 0.944 s.
- **1.26× faster than pre-WASM #115**. In that separate comparison, seed 0: #115 1.231 s, JavaScript 1.007 s.
- All **30 paired comparisons** have identical geometry SHA-256, negotiation rounds, and search expansions. All seeds still solve at 1× with zero configured-clearance violations.

These are local Bun 1.4.1 isolated-node timings; the two comparisons ran separately. Raw measurements and reproduction commands are committed in `docs/a13-javascript-vs-wasm.json`, `docs/a13-javascript-vs-pr115.json`, and `docs/a13-negotiated-congestion.md`. This is an experiment for review, not a performance-neutral replacement claim.

### Validation

- Full suite: **104 passed, 2 existing skips, 0 failures**.
- Type checking, library build, formatting, and diff checks passed locally.
- JavaScript and C/WASM agree at every debugger step, including fractional budgets, non-contiguous layers, exhausted frontiers, every provisional route change, and each round's ordered geometry findings.
- The default backend is tested with WASM initialization blocked and makes zero initialization attempts.
- Cosmos fixture verified with JavaScript: 26/26 routes, zero conflicts, 34 rounds, 4,079,934 expansions; one browser run completed in 0.954 s.

title: fix: accept capacitors inline with horizontal traces
description: Fixes capacitor orientation warnings for capacitors placed inline with horizontal traces, allowing for better readability of signal flow in schematics.
body:
The repro merged in #58 places C1 between R1 and R2 on a horizontal signal path. CapacitorOrientationSolver currently reports CapacitorSymbolHorizontal from the symbol orientation alone, so it recommends rotating a capacitor even when the horizontal orientation keeps the signal flow readable.

This change makes the exception depend on the rendered schematic geometry.

### Behavior

- Require exactly two rendered capacitor ports and an attached trace leaving each port horizontally in its facing direction.
- Accept the horizontal orientation when at least one side continues as a straight horizontal run.
- Do not treat a bend farther downstream as a capacitor-orientation problem; rotating the capacitor would not remove that bend.
- Keep reporting unconnected capacitors and layouts where both connected traces route away from the horizontal run.
- Preserve the existing direct op-amp feedback exception.
- Keep rail-connected horizontal components covered by the existing TwoPinComponentShouldBeVertical analysis.

The check uses schematic ports and trace edges already present in Circuit JSON. It does not match component names, net names, pin numbers, or absolute circuit coordinates.

The #58 expected-failure test is now a normal passing test. A second TSX-rendered control offsets the downstream stage to create a real bent trace and confirms that the distant bend does not produce a false capacitor-orientation warning.

title: Use actual trace width when pushing copper away from pads
description: Fixes DRC violations by using the actual trace width for copper repulsion from pads, reducing pad-to-trace errors from 6 to 0.
body:
Broad obstacle repulsion used `srj.minTraceWidth / 2` for every trace. A 0.15 mm trace on a 0.1 mm-minimum board could settle at 0.09 mm pad clearance despite a 0.1 mm rule. This contributed to pad DRCs in [bug report f6cc2bb3](https://api.tscircuit.com/autorouting/bug_reports/view?autorouting_bug_report_id=f6cc2bb3-c4bd-4f2f-ac41-5b11470e4234).

Use each segment's copper radius for the repulsion distance and the maximum segment radius for the spatial query envelope. This keeps wider copper in neighboring buckets discoverable without over-pushing thinner traces.

Validation:

- Three focused regressions check actual trace width and a spatial-bucket boundary. They preserve trace width, fixed endpoints, and input geometry. The original code fails the width regression; restoring only the undersized query fails the bucket regression.
- All 94 tests pass; `bun run typecheck` passes.
- Replayed the captured report's broad-repair stage against the same input and reference evaluator: 10 total DRCs become 4, with pad-to-trace errors reduced from 6 to 0. The remaining trace/trace and via/trace reports are unchanged.

The clearance calculation retains the original addition order for minimum-width traces. A stability regression passes on the original pin, fails when the additions are reassociated, and passes with the corrected order. This avoids perturbing existing repair decisions while correcting wider copper.

This PR targets `perf/repair-net-lookup-autorouter-pin`, the development line currently pinned by the autorouter (`fd77be86`), so the consumer can adopt this fix without changing unrelated repair behavior. The algorithm change can also be ported to main.

title: Fix terminal via escapes ignoring declared pad clearance
description: Fixes terminal via escape calculations to respect declared pad clearance, ensuring proper clearance in PCB designs.
body:
Stacked on #117. Merge the repro first, then this fix; the repro alone deliberately preserves the bug.

## Root cause

The safe terminal escape generator searched only for via radius plus epsilon, and its final acceptance check likewise ignored the requested copper-edge clearance. Connected pads are exempt from general same-net DRC, so the illegal placement survived.

## Fix

Use via radius + the existing configured/default via-to-pad clearance + epsilon for the search, sufficient outer search bound, and acceptance check. Keep the explicit via-in-pad operation separate and unchanged. No router flags, route edits, board-specific offsets, or dependency changes are used to mask the defect.

The real USB-C circuit from #117 now has approximately 0.100001 mm clearance at both the connector and fuse terminal vias instead of approximately 0.000001 mm. Its ordinary PCB SVG changes in this diff. The existing terminal-escape snapshot also changes because it now honors the same default gap.

## Verification

- 90 tests / 706 assertions pass.
- Both typechecks and repository formatcheck pass.
- Real-circuit assertions measure native polygon/rectangle pads against final native via lands.
- Additional regression uses that same real circuit input and real DRC error for default, zero, 0.1, 0.25, and 4 mm gaps, diagonal escapes, and rejection outside board bounds.
- PCB-port coordinates/identities and unrelated routes remain unchanged.
- Existing explicit via-in-pad and drill-containment tests pass.

This is a focused terminal-generation fix, not a claim that all board blockers or all same-net via DRC policies are resolved. The separate connector mechanical-hole contact remains documented and visible in the native reproduction output.

title: parse and render parameter set directives (record 43)
description: Implements a dedicated AltiumSchParameterSetRecord for schematic RECORD43, registers it to eliminate fallback to AltiumUnknownRecord, adds convenience getters, and enables native SVG rendering for parameter set directives.
body:
## Summary

- Implements a dedicated `AltiumSchParameterSetRecord` (and alias `AltiumSchDifferentialPairRecord`) for schematic `RECORD=43`.
- Registers `RECORD=43` in `recordConstructors` to eliminate fallback to `AltiumUnknownRecord`.
- Adds `parameterSets` and `differentialPairs` convenience getters to `AltiumSchDoc`.
- Adds native SVG rendering for parameter set / differential pair directives (draws connection marker circle and directive name text).

## Background

In Altium schematic documents (`.SchDoc`), `RECORD=43` represents a Parameter Set directive (such as Differential Pair directives like `DIFFPAIR` or net class directives like `1A`). Previously, these records had no dedicated class and parsed as `AltiumUnknownRecord`, leaving directives unrendered in SVG outputs.

## Changes

- **`lib/records/altium-schematic-records.ts`**:
  - Added `name`, `color`, and `isDifferentialPair` accessors to `AltiumSchParameterSetRecord`.
  - Exported `AltiumSchDifferentialPairRecord` alias.
- **`lib/parser/record-constructors.ts`**:
  - Registered `"43": AltiumSchParameterSetRecord`.
- **`lib/altium-sch-doc.ts`**:
  - Added `parameterSets` and `differentialPairs` getters.
- **`lib/svg-serialization/serialize-altium-sheet-to-svg.ts`**:
  - Rendered `RECORD=43` directive marker and label.
- **`tests/schematic-parameter-set.test.ts`**:
  - Unit tests for AST parsing, ownership, and round-trip preservation.
- **`tests/svg/schematic-parameter-set.test.ts`**:
  - Added SVG snapshot test for schematic differential pair directives.
- **Updated snapshots**:
  - `tests/svg/__snapshots__/schematic-component-value-reference.snap.svg` (now includes `DIFFPAIR` directives from `stm32-st-link-v2.SchDoc`).
  - `tests/svg/__snapshots__/schematic-note-text-frame-repro.snap.svg` (now includes `1A` directive marker from `pidp11-io-expander.SchDoc`).

title: Add native scoped keepout exclusion rules (needs Altium DRC verification)
description: Adds native scoped clearance rules for keepouts with excluded PCB component IDs, improving the handling of clearance violations in Altium Designer.
body:
Exporting [fitness_watch](https://tscircuit.com/imrishabh18/fitness_watch#schematic) aborts on the ESP-12E/U2 keepout's `excluded_pcb_component_ids`. This proposes native scoped clearance rules instead of the warning fallback in #145. It is based directly on main and does not include that fallback.

Each exempt keepout receives a distinct union index, shared by its primitives across layers. A native Clearance rule targets `IsKeepOut And InUnion(n)` against the excluded components and traces on their connected nets. Other component pads and polygon pours are not exempted merely because they share those nets. The connected-trace scope follows tscircuit's `checkEachPcbTraceNonOverlapping` behavior.

A binary serialization bridge writes the `Rules6` stream and native fill/track/region union fields omitted by the pinned altiumts writer. Ordinary keepouts retain their existing export path. No keepouts are removed and no warning fallback is added. Invalid or ambiguous query names fail closed.

### Merge blocker: native behavior must be verified

The rule currently uses `GAP=0mil`, following [Altium's documented local clearance treatment for footprint keepout conflicts](https://www.altium.com/documentation/knowledge-base/altium-designer/keepout-region-error-within-the-same-footprint-primitives). That guidance alone does not prove that the rule permits all required overlaps or interactive routing through a keepout. **This draft is not yet a demonstrated semantic fix.** A zero clearance may still leave a collision restriction in place.

Before merging, test in Altium Designer:
- U2's pads and traces connected to its pins can cross its keepout without clearance violations or routing blockage.
- Unrelated traces, pads and pours remain restricted.
- U2 remains restricted by another non-exempt keepout, even if it occupies the same location.
- Rectangle, circle and outline keepouts behave consistently on their specified layers.

If zero clearance does not permit the required crossings, revise the native representation before marking this ready. Do not treat viewer rendering or parsed rule fields as proof of DRC behavior.

### Validation completed

- TypeScript and changed-file formatting checks passed.
- Seven focused keepout/annotation/cutout tests passed. Additional native tests verify rule scopes, union bytes, per-keepout isolation, unchanged geometry, invalid references and query names.
- Generated the real fitness_watch project with the native rule and successfully reparsed its binary PCB.
- Loaded the ZIP in https://altiumts.vercel.app/ and verified both the PCB and schematic render with 37 components. The viewer offers rendering, not Altium routing/clearance evaluation.
- Full regression suite and Altium Designer behavioral verification are not claimed.

References: [Altium membership queries](https://www.altium.com/documentation/altium-designer/pcb/query-functions/membership-checks), [KiCad's Altium binary parser](https://github.com/KiCad/kicad-source-mirror/blob/master/pcbnew/pcb_io/altium/altium_parser_pcb.cpp).

title: Compare SVG snapshot pixels instead of raw bytes
description: Changes the SVG snapshot comparison method to visually compare rendered images instead of relying on raw byte equality, improving accuracy in detecting changes in SVG snapshots.
body:
SVG snapshot checks can fail even when the rendered board is unchanged. Asynchronous footprint loading can change generated IDs and the order of independent SVG elements; the AP3429A snapshot failure in https://github.com/tscircuit/sparkfun-boards/pull/328 is one example. Plain `tsci snapshot` compares raw buffers, and the image comparator used by `--ci`/`--test` also falls back to byte equality for SVG input because it only decodes PNGs.

Render differing SVGs to PNGs with the existing Resvg helper before comparing them. Use this visual comparison for normal checks as well as checks that produce diff artifacts. Identical buffers take a fast path, and explicit `--update` without diff generation continues to refresh metadata and other nonvisual SVG text. SVG mismatch artifacts remain SVG files; PNG diff generation is preserved.

Regression coverage verifies that changed IDs, comments, and reordered non-overlapping elements pass, while changed colors and reordered overlapping shapes fail. CLI tests cover normal, `--ci`, and `--test` checks, explicit updates, and real visual mismatches. The captured AP3429A SVG pair has different bytes and compares equal with this change.

The comparison uses the SVG's native rendered dimensions and the existing tolerance of 2. This makes snapshot validation visual; it does not promise to detect subpixel geometry changes or make Circuit JSON generation deterministic.

- 12 targeted tests passed, including SVG equality, visual mismatch detection, metadata updates, all snapshot check modes, and PCB/schematic/3D diff artifacts.

title: Fix dense AM62L fanout finalization
description: Fixes contract failures in dense fanout finalization for the AM62L, ensuring proper routing and validation of fanout traces.
body:
## Stack

- base/repro: #213
- this PR: production fix plus the passing version of the same visual test

## Root cause and fix

The real Core handoff exposed four related contract failures in dense fanout finalization:

- the parent solver could exhaust its own iteration limit while a delegated work solver still had declared work remaining
- recovery could reroute a wide direct-exit bus before its embedded singleton, closing the singleton source corridor
- a corner-adjacent winding path could touch a different shared-boundary edge before reaching its declared exit
- a complete dense candidate was normalized and validated, then passed through generic finalization transformations a second time

This change makes those contracts explicit: the parent honors the active worker budget, recovery preserves the embedded singleton corridor, exact-exit routing rejects early contact with any shared-boundary edge, and a normalized fully validated dense result is terminal without double finalization.

The pair-plan tuple narrowing is included because current main enables strict indexed access and otherwise does not typecheck; it changes no routing behavior.

## Visual result

The same exact fixture from #213 changes from an unsolved partial routing after 2,000 deterministic steps to a solved and fully validated result with 143/143 fanout traces and 110 plane terminations. The test additionally requires octilinear geometry and rejects boundary contact before each exact exit.

## Verification

- bun test tests/am62l-direct-decoupling-dram.test.ts: 1 pass, 2,455 assertions
- 12 focused AM62L, boundary-tail, reserved-exit, and winding tests: 12 pass, 1,796 assertions
- NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=4096 bun run typecheck
- Biome format check on all changed TypeScript files

Core visual repro: https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/3783

title: fix: render text associated with custom schematic components
description: Fixes the issue where external schematic text associated with custom components disappears from the schematic SVG when is_box_with_pins is false.
body: Fixes #739. External `schematic_text` associated with a custom component (`is_box_with_pins: false`) disappears from the schematic SVG. Removing only `schematic_component_id` makes the same label visible. This prevents callers from keeping the component association while also displaying an independently positioned reference label. The main rendering loop skips component-associated text because component renderers own it. However, the custom-component primitives renderer handles lines, circles, rectangles, arcs, and paths without handling text, so these labels fall through both rendering paths. Render associated text through `createSvgSchText` in the primitives renderer when `is_box_with_pins` is false. This preserves the supplied position and text styling. The condition leaves box-component text with its existing renderer, preventing duplicate labels, and does not change embedded symbol-text rendering. The regression test uses the existing AMS1117-3.3 custom symbol for [JLCPCB C6186](https://jlcpcb.com/partdetail/AMS1117-3.3/C6186), scaled for readability, with an external reference matching the source-component name. This is a real-part reproduction of the reported behavior, not the reporter's original circuit (none was attached). It includes an SVG snapshot for the custom component and assertions for both custom and box components, reproduces the original failure, verifies that an associated label produces the same text SVG as an unassociated label, and checks that both custom and box components render it exactly once.
